english.title: Sponsor fail to ensure the recording and reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions in a clinical trial

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial, failed to ensure that all relevant information about a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction, which occurred during the course of the clinical trial in the United Kingdom and was fatal or life-threatening was

(A)_[recorded]_
(B)_[reported as soon as possible]_
(C)_[recorded and reported as soon as possible]_

and in any event not later than 7 days after you were first aware of the reaction, to the

(D)_[licensing authority,]_
(E)_[competent authorities of the EEA State, in which the trial was being conducted,]_
(F)_[relevant ethics committee,]_
(G)_[**(..SPECIFY A COMBINATION OF THE ABOVE..),]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF AUTHORITY / COMMITTEE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 33(1), 49(1)(h) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 49 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 makes a breach of reg 33 an offence.
(ii) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.
(iii) The legislation was amended as a result of the EU Exit. For offences from 1st January 2021, see H22173.
